newsitem.title: USA: Deputies begin removing items from Simpson's home.
newsitem.headline: Deputies begin removing items from Simpson's home.

text.p: Sheriff's deputies began removing $400,000 worth of art, jewels and other items from O.J. Simpson's home on Friday, one day after a judge ordered him to turn over the possessions to satisfy part of the civil award against him.
Sgt. Noel Lanier of the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department said officials arrived at Simpson's home in the posh community of Brentwood early on Friday with a moving van.
"To my knowledge, Mr. Simpson is there and is cooperating," he said.

A civil jury in February found Simpson liable for the deaths of his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman. It awarded $33.5 million in damages to the estate of Nicole Brown and Goldman's parents, Fred Goldman and Sharon Rufo.
Among the items being removed were several pieces of football memorabilia, including the Heisman Trophy, a Buffalo Bills football helmet, four football jerseys, and 10 commemorative footballs.

They were also taking a number of art works in the likeness of Simpson, including an Andy Warhol silkscreen entitled "O.J. Simpson," a metal sculpture of the former football star and a large photograph.
Simpson also was ordered to turn over several Tiffany lamps, jewels, glassware, a 1996 Chevrolet Suburban and framed congratulatory letters from Richard Nixon.
Superior Court Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki entered the order this week after Fred Goldman submitted a list of more than 100 items he wanted turned over to the court to prevent Simpson from selling them.
Fujisaki ordered Simpson to surrender the property to the sheriff's department, and "let the parties fight it out," over who gets what.
